instruction: Open C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_037_replace_component_assembly.step, C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_037_new_motor.step in SolidWorks. Using SolidWorks command-line automation, use input file C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_037_replace_component_assembly.step and C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_037_new_motor.step. The assembly contains a frame plate, old_motor, and a coupler. The frame plate spans X=-30..70, Y=-35..35, Z=0..8 and has four 6 mm mounting holes at (X,Y)=(25,-20), (25,20), (55,-20), and (55,20). Remove old_motor from the assembly and insert the new motor. Place the new motor so its mounting holes align to the frame holes, its bottom face sits on the frame top face at Z=8, and its shaft axis is coaxial with the coupler axis at Y=0, Z=30. Preserve frame and coupler geometry and avoid new interference. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_037_replaced_motor_out.step containing frame, new_motor, and coupler only. [Software] Launch SOLIDWORKS from `C:\Program Files\SOLIDWORKS Corp\SOLIDWORKS\` (use your actual executable or shortcut). Run the SOLIDWORKS automation through `C:\Program Files\SOLIDWORKS Corp\SOLIDWORKS\SLDWORKS.exe` when working on `cli_037_replace_component_assembly.step`.
